content: A Diploma in Nursing, also referred to as a Nursing Diploma, is an entry-level tertiary education credential in the field of nursing. In the United States, this type of degree is typically conferred by hospital-based nursing schools. Individuals who earn a Diploma in Nursing are eligible to take the NCLEX-RN examination and apply for licensure as a Registered Nurse (RN). Historically, all nurses in the United States were trained through diploma programs. During World War II, the Cherry Ames series of children's books was created to inspire young girls to pursue careers in nursing. The protagonist of the series was depicted as a hospital diploma nurse, reflecting the common educational pathway for nurses at the time. Although the number of hospital-based nursing schools has been steadily declining, many such programs still exist. Some of these programs require students to complete non-nursing prerequisite courses at other institutions prior to admission, or they coordinate their curriculum with classes offered at nearby schools. However, many hospital-based nursing programs remain self-contained, providing all necessary coursework and training within their own structure.
